title: Shivam Is Back: Awarapan 2 Teaser Drops 19 Years to the Day — and Emraan Hashmi Has Never Looked More Dangerous
excerpt: The cult classic gets its sequel with Disha Patani, Shabana Azmi, and the return of 'Toh Phir Aao' — releasing this Independence Day
body:
There are comebacks, and then there is **Emraan Hashmi** walking back into a role that an entire generation refused to let go of.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=IQ7HkZ-Gun8</youtube>

The teaser for **Awarapan 2** landed today — June 29, 2026 — exactly nineteen years after the original slipped into cinemas, flopped at the box office, and then spent two decades becoming one of the most quietly beloved Hindi films ever made. The timing is deliberate. Producer **Vishesh Bhatt** chose the anniversary to mark the return of Shivam Pandit, the brooding, broken-hearted gangster who made Emraan more than just the serial-kisser tag Bollywood had pinned on him.

And from the first frames of the teaser, it is clear this is not a nostalgia cash-grab.

https://www.instagram.com/reel/DaKH7R2MMFc/

Emraan looks older, leaner, and considerably more dangerous. The Shivam we knew was a man trapped between loyalty and love. The Shivam we are about to meet seems to have chosen violence — and the teaser leans into that darkness with a visual palette that is all rain-soaked alleyways, amber light, and close-ups of a face that has clearly seen too much. There is a shot of him walking through what appears to be a Bangkok night market, collar up, jaw set, and it is the kind of frame that reminds you why this man was once Bollywood's most compelling antihero.

## The Cast That Changes Everything

**Disha Patani** steps in as the female lead, and the pairing is unexpected in the best way. Where the original's Reema (played by the luminous Mrinalini Sharma) was fragile and captive, Disha's character — from the little the teaser reveals — seems to carry her own edge. The real casting coup, though, is **Shabana Azmi** as Nafisa. Vishesh Bhatt personally welcomed the veteran aboard in June, calling her "an important part of the Awarapan world." Azmi in a Vishesh Films thriller is the kind of combination that promises something far more layered than the average sequel.

Director **Nitin Kakkar** — best known for the National Award-winning *Filmistaan* — takes over from Mohit Suri, who helmed the original. It is a curious but intriguing choice: Kakkar's sensibility tends toward the grounded and humanist, which could give the sequel's emotional beats a rawness that the first film sometimes smoothed over with style.

## The Music Will Break You

If you grew up playing *Toh Phir Aao* on loop during your first heartbreak, brace yourself. **Mithoon** and lyricist **Sayeed Quadri** — the original's musical architects — are back to compose the sequel's album. And they are not just writing new tracks. Both *Toh Phir Aao* and *Tera Mera Rishta* are getting reimagined versions, designed to hit the same nerve while sounding like they belong in 2026.

> "We spent nearly two years refining the script to ensure the sequel lives up to the emotional depth of the original. This is not nostalgia — it is a continuation." — Emraan Hashmi

The promotional blitz begins now. The makers have planned a month-long campaign leading up to the August 14 release — right in the heart of the Independence Day weekend. It will not be a solo run, though: **Sunny Deol's** partition drama *Lahore 1947*, produced by Aamir Khan, arrives a day earlier on August 13. Two very different films, two very different audiences, and a box-office clash that could define the second half of 2026.

## Why the Diaspora Should Care

The original *Awarapan* has a peculiar afterlife among Indians abroad. It is one of those films that circulates through WhatsApp forwards, Spotify playlists, and late-night YouTube spirals — a film people discover years after release and then wonder why nobody told them sooner. Its songs are wedding-playlist staples in the UK and US desi communities. The sequel arriving with the same composer, the same producer, and the same lead is the kind of event that does not need a marketing push in NRI living rooms.

*Awarapan 2* is scheduled for a worldwide theatrical release on **August 14, 2026**. Mark it.
